_comment: Default values for user-editable Bot Config settings AND server-internal operator-tunable defaults. The dashboard reads the top-level keys at init via GET /api/bot-config-defaults and uses them as the initial input value when .bot-config.json has no explicit override. The server also falls back to these when `getConfig` is asked for a value the user hasn't set. Top-level keys match the bot-config-v2 POSITION_KEYS / GLOBAL_KEYS naming so the same string flows from this file → dashboard input → .bot-config.json → bot reader. Nested groups (lowGasThresholds, residualCleanup) are server-internal: not exposed in the Bot Settings UI, consumed directly by src/gas-monitor.js and src/bot-cycle-residual.js. ui-defaults.json, dust-threshold.json and nft-providers.json stay standalone (different concern + data shape).
_gasFeePct_bounds_comment: Validation bounds for gasFeePct (UI input min/max). Mirror to public/index.html input[min|max] attrs. Consumed by src/swap-gates.js (gasFeePctToRatio clamping) and src/bot-config-defaults.js (_NORMALIZERS.gasFeePct).
_rpcAccess_comment: RPC access plumbing. NOT exposed in the Bot Settings UI and NOT in bot-config-v2 GLOBAL_KEYS — these are operator-tunable plumbing, not user settings, and should never need changing in normal operation. Override them in app-config/user-configurable/bot-config-defaults.json and restart. The two work as a pair: chunk size decides how many requests a scan produces, the interval decides how fast they leave. See docs/engineering.md § "RPC Request Pacing and Log Chunking".
_getLogsChunkSize_comment: Max block span per eth_getLogs / queryFilter call. RPC endpoints cap this and reject anything wider; the strictest cap observed is 10000 (rpc-pulsechain.g4mm4.io, which returns JSON-RPC -32602 'eth_getLogs is limited to a 10000 block range'). Default 7500 = 75% of that, deliberately leaving headroom because endpoints keep some limits unpublished on purpose, so an observed ceiling is not a promise. Lower it if an endpoint rejects a query; the resulting error names this key. Raising it reduces total requests and therefore scan wall-clock.
_globalRPCRequestRateInterval_comment: Minimum milliseconds between ANY two JSON-RPC requests leaving this process. Every request — reads, writes, getBlockNumber, eth_call, transaction submission — queues in src/rpc-request-manager.js and is released one at a time on this schedule, so the whole process shares one budget regardless of how many providers or concurrent scans are running. Default 250 (4/s), comfortably inside the tightest published limit we know of (rpc.pulsechain.box free tier: 50 requests per 10 seconds = 5/s). Set 0 to disable pacing entirely (only sensible against a local node).
_priceCacheTtl_comment: Price-source cache TTL in milliseconds (in-memory cache inside src/price-fetcher.js, gated by the idle-driven pause). Default 120_000 (2 min) — long enough to absorb the 300 s poll cadence but short enough that a real price move shows up promptly when something's looking. The dust-unit-price cache TTL is computed at module-load as priceCacheTtlMs * dustUnitPriceCacheMultiplier, so the integer-multiple constraint is structural (a runtime assertion guards against future hand-edits).
_moveCacheTtl_comment: Price-source cache TTL while inside a withFreshPricesAllowed scope (rebalance/compound). Default 4_000 ms (4 s) — short enough that any move-relevant price change shows up but long enough to collapse the rapid-fire burst that the rebalance pipeline triggers when multiple stages (gas gate, slippage estimate, PnL snapshot, etc.) each call fetchTokenPriceUsd for the same token. Without this, a single rebalance can hit each price source 4-6× for one token in a few seconds. See src/price-fetcher.js and src/price-fetcher-gate.js#inMove.
_pricePauseExceptionPollWindowMultiple_c: Balanced-band Telegram notifier: number of bot poll cycles between fresh-price fetches that bypass the idle-driven price-lookup pause. Effective cadence = checkIntervalSec × pricePauseExceptionPollWindowMultiple seconds. Default 10 (10× poll = 50 min at the default 300 s poll). Higher = lighter price-source load, slower band-crossing detection. Positive integer >= 1. Only consulted when the 'positionBalanced' Telegram event is enabled.
_impermanentLossGuardPct_comment: Impermanent Loss Guard: the most a position may have lost before the bot stops rebalancing it, in percent. Shown in Bot Settings → Execution and per-position. The hypothetical post-rebalance position (LP value plus the pool residual it would absorb, slippage excluded) is compared against the held NFT's own USD value at its mint; the rebalance is rejected when the projection falls more than this far below it. Skipped for user-forced 'Rebalance Now' clicks. Default 50 is deliberately loose: the check only arises when a rebalance was due, which usually means the position is out of range and earning nothing, and a rejection can only clear when price recovers (a blocked position cannot mint a new NFT, so it cannot get a new baseline). A tighter value stops rebalancing during ordinary volatility. Bounded 1..100 by src/bot-config-defaults.js. Retry pacing lives in the ilGuardRetry group below.
_impermanentLossGuardPct_bounds_comment: Validation bounds for impermanentLossGuardPct — the single source for the Bot Settings input's min/max, the dashboard's Save validation, and the server-side clamp. The dashboard reads them from GET /api/bot-config-defaults and stamps them onto the input at init, so they are NOT duplicated as literal min/max attributes in public/index.html. Consumed by src/bot-config-defaults.js (_NORMALIZERS.impermanentLossGuardPct) and public/dashboard-init.js. 1 is the tightest meaningful guard; 100 effectively disables it, since the position would have to be worthless to trip it.
_rebalanceRangeWidthPct_comment: Default Price Range Extension (percent of current price) that the 'Default' button on the Price Range Extension row (Bot Settings → Range) applies to the input. Positions without a saved override use preserveRange() at rebalance time (existing on-chain tick spread) — this value is NOT auto-applied to the bot; it's purely the value the button injects into the input so the user can Save it with one click. Per feedback_one_literal_per_shipped_default the literal lives here only. Raised 15 → 80 on 2026-08-05 from operator experience on PulseChain: at 15 percent a volatile pair leaves range quickly, and each rebalance realizes impermanent loss and pays gas. A wider band earns a lower fee rate per unit of liquidity but goes out of range far less often, which in practice has been the better trade in these markets. Bounded 0.1..200 by src/bot-config-defaults.js (200 = the full plus/minus 100 percent span).
_fullRangeRebalanceEnabled_comment: Per-position 'Full-Range Rebalance' toggle. When true, every rebalance mints at MIN_TICK / MAX_TICK via rangeMath.fullRange(), ignoring rebalanceRangeWidthPct. Driven by the 'Full-Range' checkbox next to the Price Range Extension input. Replaces the old rebalanceRangeWidthPct === 100 full-range sentinel.
_rangeOverrideEnabled_comment: Per-position 'No Override' toggle heading Bot Settings → Range. false = re-use the position's existing on-chain range on the next rebalance (badge 'Re-Use Existing Position Range'); the Price Range Extension, Full-Range and Position Offset fields are disabled and none of them is applied. true = apply them (badge 'Use Settings Below'). This literal is the default for a position that has never been configured. A slot saved before the toggle existed keeps its settings: src/range-override.js resolveRangeOverrideEnabled() derives true when the slot already carries rebalanceRangeWidthPct, fullRangeRebalanceEnabled=true, or offsetToken0Pct. The toggle is non-destructive — it never clears those keys.

lowGasThresholds._comment: Wallet low-gas detection tunables. Used by src/gas-monitor.js to compute two tiers for the Mission Control 'Gas Running Low' / 'Gas Critical' badge and matching Telegram alerts. Formula (chain-agnostic — gas opcodes are identical across EVMs): floor_gas_units = standardSendGas × worstCaseGasFactor (one worst-case rebalance); recommended_gas_units = floor_gas_units × safetyMultiplier × managedPositionCount. Native-token threshold = gas_units × live gasPrice. Tiers: 'ok' at balance ≥ recommended; 'low' at floor ≤ balance < recommended (amber static); 'critical' at balance < floor (blinking — next rebalance will likely fail with out-of-gas). worstCaseGasFactor=91 was derived from observed PulseChain rebalance_log.json + live logs (NFT #158965→158967) covering a rebalance that fired all 3 corrective-swap iterations: remove(~209k) + primary approve(~46k) + primary swap(~243k) + 3×corrective(approve+swap ~290k each = ~870k) + mint approves(~76k) + mint(~464k) ≈ 1,911,000 gas / 21,000 send ≈ 91. safetyMultiplier=3 is the user-specified headroom factor. standardSendGas=21000 is the EVM constant for a native-token transfer with no calldata. If the JSON is missing or malformed, gas-monitor falls back to these same defaults so the guard never silently disables.

ilGuardRetry._comment: Backoff between retries of a rebalance the Impermanent Loss Guard has rejected. First retry after baseMs (14400000 = 4 h), then doubling on each consecutive rejection — 4 h, 8 h, 16 h, 32 h — until it reaches maxMs (604800000 = 7 days), which it then holds. The ladder resets the moment the Guard lets a rebalance through, so a position that recovers starts again at 4 h. Same shape as the rebalance throttle's doubling mode. The Telegram alert rides the same schedule, so a position blocked for a long stretch reports on a widening interval rather than every poll. Cost: a position that recovers inside a window waits for it to expire; a manual 'Rebalance Now' ignores the backoff entirely. Not exposed in Bot Settings — operator-tunable via this file only.

residualCleanup._comment: Automatic residual-cleanup rebalance tunables. After every successful normal or manual rebalance, if the wallet residual share of the pool batch (residual / (LP + residual)) still exceeds thresholdPct past delayMs, the bot fires exactly one cleanup rebalance to sweep residuals back into the position. The cleanup respects ALL other rebalance rules (throttle, daily cap, doubling, swap-backoff, pause). Back-to-back cleanups are prevented by a per-position flag that only clears on the next normal rebalance. Not exposed in Bot Settings — operator-tunable via this file only.
